scenarios.setup: A resolves Elvish Visionary with cards in library.
scenarios.expected: Entry commits and one pending trigger is captured; hand does not increase until that separate ability resolves.

scenarios.setup: A creature spell is countered before it can enter.
scenarios.expected: No battlefield entry occurrence and no self-entry trigger are recorded.

scenarios.setup: Two distinct instances of the same self-entry definition enter in one event.
scenarios.expected: Exactly two trigger instances, each bound to its own source generation; index deduplication cannot merge them.

scenarios.setup: A self-entry trigger is on the stack; its creature is destroyed before resolution.
scenarios.expected: The trigger still resolves for its captured controller and has no dependency on a current source object lookup.

scenarios.setup: One resolving instruction puts the creature onto the battlefield and then removes it before any priority window.
scenarios.expected: The captured self-entry trigger survives in the waiting queue and is placed after the enclosing resolution finishes.

scenarios.setup: The same card leaves and reenters after its first entry trigger has been captured.
scenarios.expected: Two generations and two occurrences produce independent trigger IDs; both can resolve, without rebinding the old trigger to the new object.

scenarios.setup: A controls a creature when it enters; B gains control of the source before its trigger resolves.
scenarios.expected: A retains control of the trigger and receives its life gain or draw.

scenarios.setup: A owns a card that enters under B control.
scenarios.expected: B controls the self-entry trigger and is its self-effect recipient; ownership is not substituted.

scenarios.setup: A creature enters while an already-applying continuous effect removes its abilities.
scenarios.expected: Post-event effective ability lookup finds no entry trigger; printed Oracle text alone cannot create it.

scenarios.setup: A fixture creature with the same self-entry ability enters with effective toughness zero.
scenarios.expected: Entry captures the trigger; state-based death occurs before placement; the waiting ability can still be placed and resolved.

scenarios.setup: A controls simultaneous draw-one and gain-three entry triggers.
scenarios.expected: A chooses their exact bottom-to-top order; both permutations are legal and recorded, even if a resulting total could coincide.

scenarios.setup: Active A and nonactive B each have one waiting ordinary entry trigger.
scenarios.expected: Place A then B; B is topmost and resolves first after all players pass.

scenarios.setup: Seats A,B,C,D remain; active player is C; all have one waiting ordinary trigger.
scenarios.expected: Placement is C,D,A,B and initial resolution order is B,A,D,C; do not start APNAP from seat-array index zero.

scenarios.setup: Several triggers arise at different points within one spell resolution without intervening priority.
scenarios.expected: All pending ordinary triggers participate in the next applicable APNAP placement process; global capture timestamp does not override controller choices.

scenarios.setup: A future trigger-on-trigger ability waits alongside ordinary triggers.
scenarios.expected: The current narrow release rejects the unavailable program; a future implementation must honor the separate second APNAP pass.
scenarios.fixtureKind: negative admission and future meta-trigger fixture

scenarios.setup: A creature remains on the battlefield across several priority/checkpoint calls.
scenarios.expected: Its self-entry trigger is not rediscovered from persistent state or by replaying the same event ID.

scenarios.setup: An optional self-entry draw fixture triggers and its controller intends to decline.
scenarios.expected: The ability is still placed on the stack; a resolution-time decision permits decline and draws zero cards. No early suppression or forced draw.
scenarios.fixtureKind: synthetic optional-self fixture; referenced real card also has unsupported other-object condition

scenarios.setup: The same optional fixture reaches resolution and its controller accepts.
scenarios.expected: The captured controller draws one; the accept/decline decision and chosen branch are durable.

scenarios.setup: A mandatory Arashin Cleric entry trigger resolves.
scenarios.expected: No fabricated decline decision exists; gain exactly three life for the captured controller.

scenarios.setup: The source and every other creature are gone before a targetless entry ability resolves.
scenarios.expected: It still resolves; a targetless ability is not rejected for lacking creature targets.

scenarios.setup: A controller leaves after capture but before placement.
scenarios.expected: Its waiting trigger is not placed on the stack.

scenarios.setup: A controller leaves while its entry trigger is already on the stack.
scenarios.expected: That noncard stack object ceases to exist; it does not become a card in a graveyard and cannot later resolve.

scenarios.setup: An entry draw-one trigger resolves for a player with an empty library.
scenarios.expected: Record the failed draw, finish ability resolution and remove it, then apply the loss checkpoint before granting priority.
scenarios.fixtureKind: source-bound integration plus existing draw-loss rules

scenarios.setup: The top entry trigger resolves while another remains underneath.
scenarios.expected: Remove only the resolved ability, process the checkpoint and give the active player priority; do not drain the whole stack automatically.

scenarios.setup: Save after trigger capture and before placement, then reopen twice.
scenarios.expected: Waiting IDs, captured controller, source generation, program digest and occurrence IDs are identical; exactly one placement occurs.
scenarios.fixtureKind: durability requirement; no new game-rule claim

scenarios.setup: Save while a controller must order two triggers.
scenarios.expected: Restore the identical choice domain, decision ID and cohort; reject duplicates, omissions, foreign IDs, newly submitted stale or unrelated commands, and attempts by another player. Exact retries of an accepted command ID return its stored receipt without repeating placement.

scenarios.setup: Save with an ability on the stack after its source left the battlefield.
scenarios.expected: Reopen and resolve using captured ability/controller context; current object lookup cannot erase or rebind it.

scenarios.setup: Export/import while an optional resolution decision is pending.
scenarios.expected: Preserve the optional continuation and effect cursor; neither autoaccept nor repeat already completed effects.
scenarios.fixtureKind: future optional fixture and durability requirement

scenarios.setup: Source body contains draw-two plus evoke, combined gain/draw, or hybrid costs.
scenarios.expected: Keep each definition unsupported until every additional behavior and cost is explicitly implemented.

scenarios.setup: A body says another creature enters or contains an intervening-if, optional other-object trigger, or reminder-bearing unsupported clause.
scenarios.expected: Do not rewrite its condition or strip remaining text to fit a mandatory self-entry recipe.

scenarios.setup: A match plan reaches a new trigger definition while its trigger core capability is unavailable.
scenarios.expected: Reject prepared execution explicitly; do not prune trigger processors as unrelated to creature roots.

scenarios.setup: Run the same source-bound event/choice transcript in full-scan, prepared-scan and prepared-indexed modes.
scenarios.expected: Compare captured instance IDs, cohorts, exact ordering choices, public observations, event transcript and final state; only explicit configuration pins may differ.

scenarios.setup: Llanowar Visionary enters and its draw trigger waits; later a legal mana-ability window occurs.
scenarios.expected: Its green tap-mana ability remains distinct from its stack-using entry trigger and obeys existing tap/summoning restrictions.
scenarios.fixtureKind: source-bound integration plus existing mana/creature rules

scenarios.setup: A future variable-source effect needs source information after the source leaves.
scenarios.expected: Use the rules-required last-known information; the initial constant-effect recipe must reject this broader body rather than freezing a guessed value.
